lens: Outbox claim-and-dispatch race, Cache::lock semantics, retry curve, ws:heartbeat observability, polling fallback cadence cap, queue lane SLO
scope: READ-ONLY operational/reliability audit; verifies that the cascade survives realistic failure modes (Pusher down, Soketi restart, queue worker crash, transient DB lock)
verdict: PASS — retry curve, polling cadence cap, and observability heartbeat are all properly wired; one SRE concern noted as RECOMMENDATION-2
executive_summary: The DispatchDomainEventsJob is a textbook outbox dispatcher: atomic claim via lockForUpdate + dispatched_at guard committed BEFORE broadcast (lines 65-86), broadcast OUTSIDE any DB transaction (lines 96-132), Phase 3a/3b release-on-failure for retry (lines 152-189). The backoff curve [1,5,15,60,300] with tries=6 yields ~6.4 min worst-case retry window per documented intent (lines 24-40) — longer than typical Pusher/Soketi restart (1-3 min) without exceeding the SLO outbox_dispatch_latency_p95 < 2s in steady state. The ws:heartbeat observability key write (lines 127-131) is the recent GOAL-CMS-2026-05-18 S-P0-A heal that closes the silent-Pusher-down blind spot. Polling fallback in KdsSyncService.js implements a triple-tier cadence (high-activity 3s / degraded 5s / disconnected 10s) with clamp floors (250ms / 4 req/s) and ceilings (60s base / 30s jitter) preventing both DoS misconfig and silent-blind misconfig.

findings.title: Outbox claim-and-dispatch is race-safe via lockForUpdate + dispatched_at guard
findings.analysis: If two queue workers grab the same domainEventId (e.g. retry overlap), Worker A acquires the row lock, sees dispatched_at=null, sets it, commits. Worker B waits for the lock, then sees dispatched_at != null and returns silently with a structured log. Broadcast happens AFTER this transaction commits — the test OutboxConcurrentWorkerDedupeTest::two_sequential_handle_calls_only_broadcast_once verifies this empirically. PASS.

findings.title: Backoff curve [1,5,15,60,300] with tries=6 covers Pusher/Soketi restart window
findings.analysis: Worst-case retry window 1+5+15+60+300+300 = 681s. Note: tries=6 means up to 5 retries between attempts; Laravel reuses the last entry of $backoff if tries exceeds count(backoff), so attempt 5→6 also waits 300s. Per the inline rationale (lines 28-38), the previous tries=5 was caught by Audit T G2 (2026-04-23) and bumped to make the 300s trailing entry actually reachable. PASS.

findings.title: ws:heartbeat write closes the silent-Pusher-down blind spot
findings.analysis: GOAL-CMS-2026-05-18 S-P0-A heal R1 SRE-001: SyncOverviewController:531 was READING `ws:heartbeat` but NOBODY was WRITING it — admin observability dashboard would stay green-emerald while Pusher silently died. The fix stamps the cache key with `now()->timestamp` after every successful broadcast, TTL 120s (> 4× the polling fallback window). Wrapped in try/catch so observability failure never breaks the outbox. PASS.

findings.title: Polling cadence cap [floor 250ms / ceiling 60s base / jitter 30s] resists owner misconfig
findings.analysis: Wave 3 P1 KDS-RED-09 + Wave 3b P1 KDS-ADV3B-04: a runaway config (e.g. disconnectedBaseMs=10 or =999999999) is clamped to the safe band 250ms..60s, jitter 0..30s. Without these clamps, owner misconfig could either weaponize the poll loop into PHP-FPM saturation (lower bound) or silently stall KDS for 11.5 days (upper bound). Sentinel: tests/js/kdsCadenceFloor.spec.js. PASS.

findings.title: Network-level errors in polling fallback do NOT halt the poll loop
findings.analysis: F-03 Lot 1.C Audit G1 fix: network-level errors (DNS, TLS, ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED) MUST not silently halt the poll loop. The catch path schedules a retry with the current cadence so the KDS self-heals once connectivity returns. Without this, a concurrent WS+HTTP outage would leave the kitchen permanently blind. PASS.

findings.title: Reconnect-storm jitter prevents thundering herd on Soketi restart
findings.analysis: NEW-02 audit G10: when the broadcasting server restarts, every KDS station receives `reconnect_storm` simultaneously. Without client-side jitter, 50+ kitchens would hit /api/admin/kds-order/sync at the same instant. A 0–500ms uniform jitter spreads the herd; breaker delay is 5–30s so 500ms is negligible UX. PASS.

findings.title: PayloadMismatchException fails-once via $this->fail() (F-3 quick-win)
findings.analysis: Contract violations are NOT retry-recoverable. Without short-circuit, 1000 bad payloads = 6000 useless messages on the high lane. The $this->fail($e) lands the job in failed_jobs immediately and the failed() callback fires once. Sentinel: tests/Feature/Sentinels/PayloadMismatchFailOnceSentinelTest.php (referenced in code comment line 182). PASS.

findings.title: KdsSyncService::sync Cache::remember TTL=5s creates a 5-second visibility floor for polling-fallback users
findings.analysis: When the WebSocket path is degraded and KDS falls back to polling, every sync call serves the 5s-cached snapshot. Combined with the polling cadence (3-10s), worst case visibility latency in degraded mode is ~15s (10s poll + 5s cache). For V1 single-restaurant kitchen this is acceptable. Two mitigations exist in code: (a) WS-connected mode bypasses polling cadence (interval=Infinity, line 294); (b) reconnect_storm triggers a forceSync that hits the same cache, so stations see the stale 5s view simultaneously — acceptable.
findings.recommendation: V1.x: when polling is the *primary* path (Pusher disabled entirely via BROADCAST_DRIVER=null in single-restaurant low-cost deploy), consider TTL=1s to halve the worst-case latency. Not blocking V1 ship.

keep_as_is: DispatchDomainEventsJob 3-phase pattern (claim / broadcast / finalize) — textbook outbox.
